findings.text: — the negative control cannot fail as stated for the first two cases: a brief whose file is gone makes the queued launch raise `CrewError: the brief '<path>' is not readable`, `_stamp_failure` records that text on the pointer, and the next admission pass holds the request through `_retry_backoff_hold` in `reckon/crew/admission/holds.py` → `record_hold(pointer, "held-on-retry-backoff", ...)`, whose reason reads `last attempt failed: CrewError: the brief '<path>' is not readable: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<path>'; not retried before <instant>`, and `obligations._live_item` publishes that reason on the queued row under the `held-on-retry-backoff:` verdict — so the base revision already names the brief's path and states the file is missing.

— because base already publishes the path and the missing-file reading, only the deliverable's third clause (naming the reviewed run) is behaviour the node would add, while the deliverable and both control arms are stated over all three; the gate as written goes green at base on the path-and-missing half and red only on wording, so it cannot separate changed behaviour from unchanged behaviour and a node can satisfy the control without the new reading existing.
